blocks.text: Telecom Technician — Diploma in Electronics & Communication

blocks.label: Career category
blocks.text: Engineering, Technology & Computing
EDUCATION PATHWAY
Diploma in Electronics & Communication Engineering
Typically a 3-year diploma after Class 10, depending on the institution and entry route.
CAREER AREA
Telecommunications & Networking
Mobile networks, fibre-optic connectivity, broadband, telecom equipment and field maintenance.

A Telecom Technician installs, tests, maintains and troubleshoots communication equipment and network infrastructure. The technician helps ensure reliable voice, data and internet connectivity across mobile networks, fibre-optic systems, broadband networks and enterprise communication systems.
Typical responsibilities

items.text: Install and maintain telecom equipment and communication cables.
Assist with fibre-optic cable laying, splicing and testing.
Support mobile tower and base-station maintenance.
Test network connections and troubleshoot signal or connectivity problems.
Inspect routers, switches, modems, antennas and transmission equipment.
Record faults, maintenance activities and service-restoration details.
Coordinate with network engineers, field teams and service providers.
Follow electrical, tower-work, optical-fibre and site safety procedures.

blocks.label: Common workplaces
blocks.text: telecom operators, internet service providers, fibre-network contractors, telecom equipment vendors, data centres, enterprise networking teams and managed network service companies.
Stage 1 — Class 10
Develop mathematics, physics, basic electronics and problem-solving skills.
Stage 2 — Diploma in Electronics & Communication Engineering
Study electronic circuits, communication systems, digital electronics, signals, transmission lines, antennas, networking and instrumentation.
Stage 3 — Practical training
Gain supervised experience with fibre-optic systems, telecom equipment, network testing, installation and troubleshooting.
Stage 4 — Entry-level employment
Apply for Telecom Technician, Fibre Technician, Broadband Technician, Network Support Technician or Telecom Field Technician positions.
Year 1 — Electronics and communication fundamentals
Focus on understanding electronic systems and the principles behind communication networks.

items.text: Learn electrical fundamentals, electronic components and circuit analysis.
Study analog and digital electronics.
Understand basic communication systems and signal transmission.
Learn digital logic, microprocessors and basic instrumentation.
Practise using multimeters, oscilloscopes and signal generators in a supervised lab.
Develop computer literacy and basic IP networking knowledge.

blocks.text: Practical assignments

items.text: Assemble and test a basic electronic circuit.
Observe and measure signals using an oscilloscope.
Create a block diagram of a communication system.
Prepare a simple report comparing analog and digital communication.

blocks.text: Year 2 — Telecom systems and network infrastructure
Focus on the technologies used to transmit voice and data.

items.text: Learn fibre-optic communication, optical transmitters and receivers.
Understand fibre connectors, patch panels, cable routing and splicing concepts.
Study antennas, radio-frequency fundamentals and wireless communication.
Learn IP addressing, subnetting, Ethernet and basic routing concepts.
Understand mobile network architecture, including base stations and backhaul.
Study telecom power systems, backup batteries and equipment grounding.
Practise structured fault diagnosis and maintenance documentation.

blocks.text: Practical assignments

items.text: Design a small office network and IP-addressing plan.
Create a fibre-network layout for a sample building.
Document a simulated broadband fault and troubleshooting sequence.
Compare copper, fibre and wireless transmission for different use cases.

blocks.text: Year 3 — Field readiness and specialisation
Focus on real-world troubleshooting, installation standards and technical documentation.

items.text: Practise fibre-optic testing concepts and use of an optical power meter.
Learn OTDR testing principles and interpretation of sample traces.
Understand telecom equipment installation, rack layout and cable management.
Learn basic network monitoring and incident reporting.
Study mobile network concepts such as LTE and 5G architecture.
Complete industrial training or an internship with a telecom or networking organisation.
Practise customer communication, service tickets and maintenance reports.

blocks.text: Final-year project ideas

items.text: Fibre-optic connectivity plan for a campus.
Small enterprise network with router and switch configuration.
Telecom fault-management tracker using Excel.
Demonstration of optical communication using an educational kit.
Network availability dashboard using sample or simulated data.

rows.text: Electronics
Circuits, electronic components, digital logic and signal measurement
Fibre optics
Fibre types, connectors, splicing concepts, loss measurement and testing
Networking
Ethernet, TCP/IP, IPv4/IPv6 fundamentals, subnetting and basic routing
Wireless communication
Antennas, RF fundamentals, signal strength and interference
Mobile networks
LTE, 5G concepts, base stations, backhaul and network elements
Telecom equipment
Racks, patch panels, routers, switches, modems and transmission equipment
Troubleshooting
Fault isolation, testing sequences, incident records and escalation
Power systems
Backup power, batteries, grounding and safe equipment handling
Documentation
Network diagrams, asset registers, maintenance logs and service tickets
Safety
PPE, electrical precautions, fibre handling and authorised work-at-height procedures

blocks.text: Network simulation
Cisco Packet Tracer or equivalent tools for practising IP addressing, switching, routing and network troubleshooting.
Network diagnostics
Wireshark for packet analysis, ping and traceroute utilities for connectivity checks, and approved network-monitoring tools.
Telecom testing instruments
Optical power meter, OTDR, fibre inspection tools, fibre splicer, multimeter and RF test equipment as relevant to the role.
Excel and technical documentation
Maintain network inventory, fault logs, service reports, maintenance schedules and equipment records.
Fibre-Optic Technician
Installs, splices, tests and troubleshoots fibre links used in broadband, enterprise and telecom networks.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: students who enjoy hands-on fieldwork, precision and testing instruments.
Mobile Network Technician
Supports installation and maintenance of mobile network equipment, antennas, base stations and related infrastructure.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: students interested in wireless communication and field operations.
Network Support Technician
Troubleshoots connectivity, configures basic network equipment and assists with enterprise network support.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: students who prefer networking, computers and systematic fault diagnosis.
Telecom Testing Technician
Assists with equipment testing, signal measurements, fault verification and quality documentation.

blocks.label: Best suited to
blocks.text: students who prefer laboratory work, measurement and technical analysis.
Choose courses based on the specialisation and employers you plan to target.

blocks.label: Fibre-optic installation and testing
blocks.text: connector handling, splicing, loss testing and OTDR fundamentals.

blocks.label: CCNA-level networking preparation
blocks.text: networking fundamentals, switching, routing and troubleshooting; the official certification has its own examination requirements.

blocks.label: Broadband and FTTH training
blocks.text: fibre-to-the-home installation, optical distribution and customer-premises equipment.

blocks.label: Mobile network fundamentals
blocks.text: LTE/5G architecture, radio access networks and telecom backhaul.

blocks.label: Wireless and RF fundamentals
blocks.text: antennas, signal measurement and interference concepts.

blocks.label: Occupational safety
blocks.text: work-at-height training where relevant, PPE, electrical safety and site-specific procedures.

Prioritise hands-on training and check whether a course is recognised by the intended employer. A course certificate does not automatically authorise work on restricted telecom infrastructure or at height.
Look for supervised training with:

items.text: Telecom operators and their field-service partners.
Fibre-optic installation and broadband service companies.
Internet service providers.
Telecom equipment vendors and maintenance contractors.
Enterprise IT and networking teams.
Data centres and network operations support teams.
Electronics testing and communication-equipment manufacturers.

blocks.text: During an internship, aim to learn:

items.text: How network diagrams and cable routes are interpreted.
How fibre links and connectivity are tested.
How network equipment is installed and documented.
How technicians isolate and report faults.
How service tickets and restoration times are recorded.
How field safety and customer-site procedures are followed.

rows.text: Entry level
Telecom Trainee, Fibre Technician Trainee, Broadband Technician
Early career
Telecom Technician, FTTH Technician, Network Support Technician
With demonstrated competence
Senior Telecom Technician, Fibre Splicing Technician, Network Field Technician
Advanced technical roles
Network Operations Technician, RF Technician, Telecom Testing Specialist
Longer-term progression
Field Team Leader, Telecom Site Supervisor, Network Operations Supervisor

blocks.text: Progression depends on practical skills, relevant experience, employer requirements and any role-specific training or certification.
Examples of organisations and industry groups to research include:

items.text: Telecom operators such as Airtel, Jio and Vodafone Idea.
Telecom equipment and networking vendors such as Ericsson, Nokia and Cisco.
Fibre-optic contractors, broadband providers and internet service providers.
Data centres, enterprise IT service providers and network maintenance companies.
Telecom infrastructure providers and managed network service organisations.

blocks.text: These are examples to investigate, not confirmation of current vacancies. Look for entry-level technician, field technician, fibre technician and network support positions on official career pages and recognised apprenticeship channels.
Suggested portfolio contents

items.text: A network diagram for a small office or campus.
A sample fibre-optic link budget or loss-calculation exercise.
A network configuration and troubleshooting lab report.
A simulated fault log with diagnostic steps and resolution.
An equipment inventory and preventive-maintenance register.
A final-year telecom or networking project report.
Internship records and relevant training certificates.

blocks.text: Use simulated or authorised lab examples. Do not publish customer data, telecom network credentials, restricted network maps or confidential operator information.
Telecom infrastructure is evolving with higher-capacity fibre, 5G deployment, private wireless networks and increasingly software-managed infrastructure. A technician can build toward:

items.text: Fibre network testing and maintenance.
5G radio-access and backhaul support.
Enterprise networking and network administration.
Data-centre connectivity.
Network monitoring and operations support.
Telecom equipment testing and quality assurance.
IoT connectivity and industrial communication systems.

blocks.label: Recommended strategy
blocks.text: Learn fibre optics and IP networking together. This combination provides a useful foundation for both field telecom roles and future network-support opportunities.
Tick off each milestone as it is completed.
Employability milestones
0 of 10
Understand electronic circuits and communication fundamentals.
Interpret basic telecom and network diagrams.
Learn IP addressing, Ethernet and subnetting.
Complete a supervised fibre-optic or networking lab.
Practise network troubleshooting and fault documentation.
Learn relevant testing instruments and their safe use.
Complete an internship or practical training programme.
Build at least two documented telecom or networking projects.
Prepare a technical resume and portfolio.
Apply for suitable technician and trainee positions.
Reset checklist
By the end of the diploma and practical training, a job-ready candidate should be able to:

items.text: Explain fundamental electronic and communication systems.
Understand fibre-optic and IP-networking basics.
Assist with telecom installation, testing and maintenance.
Troubleshoot common connectivity problems using a structured process.
Maintain accurate technical records and equipment inventories.
Follow site safety rules and work effectively with field teams.
Demonstrate practical competence through training and project work.

blocks.label: Best starting point
blocks.text: Build practical skills in fibre-optic testing and basic IP networking, complete supervised field training, and target entry-level telecom or network technician positions before specialising in mobile networks, fibre infrastructure or network operations.
